papers.title: Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine immunogenicity in inflammatory bowel disease in relation to anti-TNF therapy and age: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. We followed humoral and cellular responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination over 12 months. METHODS: In this single-centre, prospective cohort study, adults with IBD received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. Two doses were administered 28 days apart and a third dose 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed with rank-based longitudinal models and with mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. Geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 3 months, GM NT50 values were lower against BA.1 (9.0) than against wild-type (24.2) or Delta (26.9), and 13 patients (24.5%) never reached a wild-type NT50 of 1:16. Anti-TNF therapy (32/53, 60.4%) was significantly associated with faster waning. At 6 months, adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990). In 33 thrice-vaccinated patients, intercurrent infection (15/33) raised S1-RBD IgG 4.6-fold more than the third dose alone, without a measurable gain in neutralisation. In the adjusted model, IFN-γ ELISpot responses did not differ between treatment groups. DISCUSSION: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in IBD patients over 12 months.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-centre, prospective cohort study followed adults with IBD who received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. All 53 participants were infection-naive and twice-vaccinated, with follow-up at 3, 6 and 12 months.
analysis.methods: Two doses of mRNA vaccine were administered 28 days apart, with a third dose given 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed using rank-based longitudinal models and mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex.
analysis.main_results: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. The geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 6 months, the adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for monitoring vaccine responses in IBD patients on anti-TNF therapy and highlight the potential impact of age on immunogenicity. They also suggest that cellular immunity may remain robust despite reduced humoral responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and relatively small sample size. The evidence is moderate as it is based on an observational cohort study with no clinical endpoints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) over 12 months, focusing on the impact of anti-TNF therapy and age. All 53 participants seroconverted after the first two doses, with peak IgG levels at 3 months and a significant decline by 6 months. Anti-TNF therapy was linked to faster waning of humoral responses, while age was associated with reduced neutralisation titres. Cellular responses, measured by IFN-γ ELISpot, remained preserved. The study highlights the importance of monitoring vaccine effectiveness in IBD patients on immunomodulatory therapies and suggests that age may influence immune response. However, the findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts with clinical outcomes. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and limited sample size.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in IBD patients over 12 months.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This single-centre, prospective cohort study followed adults with IBD who received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. All 53 participants were infection-naive and twice-vaccinated, with follow-up at 3, 6 and 12 months.
elements_en.methods: Two doses of mRNA vaccine were administered 28 days apart, with a third dose given 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed using rank-based longitudinal models and mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex.
elements_en.main_results: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. The geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 6 months, the adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for monitoring vaccine responses in IBD patients on anti-TNF therapy and highlight the potential impact of age on immunogenicity. They also suggest that cellular immunity may remain robust despite reduced humoral responses.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and relatively small sample size. The evidence is moderate as it is based on an observational cohort study with no clinical endpoints.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 接受免疫调节治疗的炎症性肠病(IBD)患者可能对疫苗接种的反应较差。本研究旨在评估IBD患者在12个月内的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 mRNA 疫苗的免疫原性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为单中心前瞻性队列研究研究,追踪了接受奥地利国家计划下mRNA 疫苗接种的IBD成人患者。所有53名参与者均为无感染史且两次接种,随访时间为3、6和12个月。
elements_zh.methods: 两剂mRNA 疫苗疫苗间隔28天接种,第三剂在第一剂后6-12个月接种。在基线和接种后3、6、12个月时,测量了S1-RBD IgG、针对野生型、Delta、Omicron BA.1和BA.2的活病毒50%中和滴度(NT50)以及IFN-γ ELISpot反应。使用基于排名的纵向模型和调整年龄和性别的混合效应模型分析了抗TNF治疗和年龄的相关性。
elements_zh.main_results: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. The geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 6 months, the adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在相对较年轻的队列研究中,抗TNF治疗和较高年龄与较低且持续时间较短的体液免疫反应相关,而细胞免疫反应似乎相对保持稳定。这些探索性关联需要在具有临床终点的更大规模队列研究中得到验证。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了对接受抗TNF治疗的IBD患者监测疫苗反应的必要性,并突出了年龄对免疫原性潜在影响的重要性。它们还表明,尽管体液免疫反应减弱,细胞免疫可能仍保持强大。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于单中心设计和相对较小的样本量。证据强度中等,因为它是基于观察性队列研究研究,且没有临床终点。

papers.title_zh: 炎症性肠病患者中严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 mRNA 疫苗的纵向免疫原性与抗TNF治疗及年龄的关系:一项前瞻性队列研究研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. We followed humoral and cellular responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination over 12 months. METHODS: In this single-centre, prospective cohort study, adults with IBD received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. Two doses were administered 28 days apart and a third dose 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed with rank-based longitudinal models and with mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. Geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 3 months, GM NT50 values were lower against BA.1 (9.0) than against wild-type (24.2) or Delta (26.9), and 13 patients (24.5%) never reached a wild-type NT50 of 1:16. Anti-TNF therapy (32/53, 60.4%) was significantly associated with faster waning. At 6 months, adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990). In 33 thrice-vaccinated patients, intercurrent infection (15/33) raised S1-RBD IgG 4.6-fold more than the third dose alone, without a measurable gain in neutralisation. In the adjusted model, IFN-γ ELISpot responses did not differ between treatment groups. DISCUSSION: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.

papers.title: Tracking SARS-CoV-2: Molecular epidemiology and surveillance in Health Region VIII, Buenos Aires, Argentina (2020–2021)
papers.abstract: To describe the classical and molecular epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in Health Region VIII (HRVIII, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina), we analyzed 120 421 respiratory samples from patients with acute respiratory infection during the first two pandemic years. Complete genome or partial spike gene sequences were obtained for phylogenetic analyses to investigate viral introductions, transmission dynamics, and genetic diversity. Substitution rates were estimated for predominant lineages. SARS-CoV-2 positivity was significantly higher in 2020 (37.4%) than in 2021 (31.9%, p < 0.001). In 2020, positivity was higher among travelers (41.7%) than residents (36.4%), a trend that reversed in 2021 (33.4% vs. 28.0%), reflecting the region's socioeconomic and touristic characteristics. The first wave peaked at epidemiological week (EW) 37 of 2020 and was dominated by lineages B.1.1.33, N.3, and B.1.499. A resurgence in early 2021 involved lineage N.5 and emerging Alpha and Lambda variants. The second wave peaked at EW 20 and featured cocirculation of Gamma and Lambda, which were later displaced by Delta after EW 31. Estimated substitution rates ranged from 2.4 × 10 −4 to 6.8 × 10 −4 substitutions/site/year across different clades. This study provides a detailed overview of SARS-CoV-2 circulation in HRVIII and underscores the importance of integrating genomic surveillance into public health systems to monitor emerging variants and support timely response strategies.

papers.title: Toward broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines: navigating viral evolution from past epidemics to future resilience
papers.abstract: SUMMARY Newly emerged highly pathogenic coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, and SARS-CoV-2, have successively triggered outbreaks worldwide over the past 25 years. Recently, several MERS-related coronaviruses have been identified from bats or pangolins. These viruses, along with previously found SARS-related coronaviruses, pose significant potential to infect humans and trigger pandemics. Therefore, it is necessary to develop broad-spectrum vaccines that can combat both currently circulating coronaviruses and those that may emerge in the future. Currently, approved COVID-19 vaccines provide strong protection against pre-Omicron variants, while their effectiveness against post-Omicron variants is reduced, and cross-protection against other potential coronaviruses remains limited. In the present review, we discuss vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as vaccine development following the outbreak. We also focus on strategies for developing broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines and provide a perspective on future directions for coronavirus vaccine development.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, and its variants, with an emphasis on developing broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines that can address both current and future viral threats. The central question is how to create vaccines that are effective against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses, to enhance pandemic resilience.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as vaccine development following the outbreak. It discusses strategies for broad-spectrum vaccine development and provides a perspective on future directions. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that broad-spectrum vaccines are necessary to combat both currently circulating coronaviruses and those that may emerge in the future. It highlights the importance of understanding viral evolution and the need for vaccines that can provide cross-protection against related species.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that current approved vaccines offer strong protection against pre-Omicron variants but have reduced effectiveness against post-Omicron variants and limited cross-protection against other potential coronaviruses. This indicates a gap in vaccine efficacy against evolving strains and related viruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing vaccines that can provide broad-spectrum protection against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses. It emphasizes the need for strategies that account for viral evolution and enhance pandemic preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines, emphasizing the need to address both current and future viral threats. It highlights the limitations of existing vaccines against post-Omicron variants and the importance of cross-protection against related species. The review discusses vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV before and after the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as strategies for creating vaccines that can combat multiple coronavirus species. It underscores the necessity of understanding viral evolution to improve pandemic resilience and vaccine effectiveness.

The central question is how to create vaccines that are effective against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses, to enhance pandemic resilience.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as vaccine development following the outbreak. It discusses strategies for broad-spectrum vaccine development and provides a perspective on future directions. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that broad-spectrum vaccines are necessary to combat both currently circulating coronaviruses and those that may emerge in the future. It highlights the importance of understanding viral evolution and the need for vaccines that can provide cross-protection against related species.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that current approved vaccines offer strong protection against pre-Omicron variants but have reduced effectiveness against post-Omicron variants and limited cross-protection against other potential coronaviruses. This indicates a gap in vaccine efficacy against evolving strains and related viruses.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing vaccines that can provide broad-spectrum protection against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses. It emphasizes the need for strategies that account for viral evolution and enhance pandemic preparedness.

papers.title_zh: 面向广谱冠状病毒疫苗:从过往疫情中应对病毒进化到未来韧性发展
papers.source_body_en: SUMMARY Newly emerged highly pathogenic coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, and SARS-CoV-2, have successively triggered outbreaks worldwide over the past 25 years. Recently, several MERS-related coronaviruses have been identified from bats or pangolins. These viruses, along with previously found SARS-related coronaviruses, pose significant potential to infect humans and trigger pandemics. Therefore, it is necessary to develop broad-spectrum vaccines that can combat both currently circulating coronaviruses and those that may emerge in the future. Currently, approved COVID-19 vaccines provide strong protection against pre-Omicron variants, while their effectiveness against post-Omicron variants is reduced, and cross-protection against other potential coronaviruses remains limited. In the present review, we discuss vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as vaccine development following the outbreak. We also focus on strategies for developing broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines and provide a perspective on future directions for coronavirus vaccine development.

papers.title: The role of personality traits in COVID-19 vaccination: A socio-cultural and gender-stratified analysis in Japan
papers.abstract: Abstract Background COVID-19 vaccination uptake is influenced by various sociodemographic and psychological factors. Previous studies have suggested that the relationship between personality traits and vaccination is context-dependent. However, this association has not been investigated in Japan—a unique sociocultural context characterized by historically low vaccine confidence but exceptionally high COVID-19 vaccine uptake. We examined the association between the Big Five personality traits and completion of the primary COVID-19 vaccination series, exploring potential gender–personality interactions. Methods A web-based, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 7,210 Japanese adults (aged 20–85 years) in December 2021. Personality was assessed using the Japanese version of the Ten-Item Personality Inventory. Multivariable Poisson generalized estimating equations were used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and assess gender–personality interactions. Results Higher extraversion and lower openness were significantly associated with vaccination completion across genders. A significant gender–agreeableness interaction was observed: agreeableness (PR = 1.016, 95% CI: 1.008–1.024) was positively associated with vaccination completion among men but not women. A similar, though only marginally significant, interaction pattern was observed for neuroticism (PR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.004–1.019 among men). Conclusions Personality traits act as modest but meaningful, gender-specific psychological modifiers of vaccination behavior in Japan. Public health campaigns should transition from traditional “one-size-fits-all” messages to personality-tailored and gender-responsive communication strategies to optimize vaccine uptake and bolster psychological resilience in future pandemics.

papers.title: Genome-wide within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection in a person with advanced HIV infection
papers.abstract: Within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection can be extensive in immunocompromised individuals, but the consequences of mutations that emerge and change in frequency over time remain difficult to predict. We characterized an XBB.1.5.10 infection lasting nearly 90 days in a person with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Genome-wide tracking of allele frequencies in samples collected on study days 43, 48, and 70 revealed a Spike N-terminal domain (NTD) deletion spanning residues 138-145 at frequencies of 33%, 80%, and 96%, respectively. A receptor-binding domain (RBD) deletion-insertion spanning residues 373-378 was detected on days 43 and 48 but not on day 70, while nsp12 C464Y was detected at approximately 8% on day 48 and 86% on day 70. We reconstructed representative Spike and non-Spike mutation profiles from the longitudinal samples and tested their effects on cell entry and viral RNA replication. The representative Spike construct for days 43 and 48 increased entry relative to XBB.1.5. Comparison with a matched construct lacking the receptor-binding domain deletion-insertion showed that the deletion-insertion enhanced entry, although it was not detected in the day 70 sample. The day 48 non-Spike profile supported the highest RNA replication among the tested replicons. Together, allele-frequency tracking revealed both transient mutations and mutations detected at progressively higher frequencies across the sampled time points. Functional testing showed that increased entry or RNA replication in vitro did not necessarily predict persistence in vivo.

source_records.title: Genome-wide within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection in a person with advanced HIV infection
source_records.abstract: Within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection can be extensive in immunocompromised individuals, but the consequences of mutations that emerge and change in frequency over time remain difficult to predict. We characterized an XBB.1.5.10 infection lasting nearly 90 days in a person with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Genome-wide tracking of allele frequencies in samples collected on study days 43, 48, and 70 revealed a Spike N-terminal domain (NTD) deletion spanning residues 138-145 at frequencies of 33%, 80%, and 96%, respectively. A receptor-binding domain (RBD) deletion-insertion spanning residues 373-378 was detected on days 43 and 48 but not on day 70, while nsp12 C464Y was detected at approximately 8% on day 48 and 86% on day 70. We reconstructed representative Spike and non-Spike mutation profiles from the longitudinal samples and tested their effects on cell entry and viral RNA replication. The representative Spike construct for days 43 and 48 increased entry relative to XBB.1.5. Comparison with a matched construct lacking the receptor-binding domain deletion-insertion showed that the deletion-insertion enhanced entry, although it was not detected in the day 70 sample. The day 48 non-Spike profile supported the highest RNA replication among the tested replicons. Together, allele-frequency tracking revealed both transient mutations and mutations detected at progressively higher frequencies across the sampled time points. Functional testing showed that increased entry or RNA replication in vitro did not necessarily predict persistence in vivo.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the within-host evolution of SARS-CoV-2 during a prolonged infection in a person with advanced HIV. The research highlights the extensive mutation patterns observed over nearly 90 days, including a Spike N-terminal domain deletion and a receptor-binding domain deletion-insertion. These mutations were tracked across different time points and showed varying frequencies. Functional testing indicated that increased entry or RNA replication in vitro did not always correlate with in vivo persistence. The findings contribute to understanding how mutations affect viral behavior in immunocompromised hosts, which has implications for surveillance and treatment strategies. However, the study's results are based on a single case, limiting generalizability and the strength of the evidence.

papers.abstract_zh: 在免疫功能低下的个体中,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2在长期感染期间的全基因组突变可以广泛存在,但随时间推移而出现并频率变化的突变对感染后果的影响仍难以预测。我们描述了一名晚期HIV感染者中持续近90天的XBB.1.5.10感染情况。在研究第43、48和70天采集的样本中进行全基因组等位基因频率追踪,发现刺突蛋白N端结构域(NTD)缺失覆盖残基138-145,其频率分别为33%、80%和96%。在第43和48天检测到覆盖残基373-378的受体结合域(RBD)缺失-插入突变,但在第70天未检测到;同时,在第48天检测到nsp12 C464Y突变频率约为8%,在第70天则升至86%。我们从纵向样本中重建了代表性的刺突蛋白和非刺突蛋白突变谱系,并测试了它们对细胞进入和病毒RNA复制的影响。第43和48天的代表性刺突蛋白构建体相较于XBB.1.5增强了细胞进入能力。与缺乏RBD缺失-插入突变的匹配构建体相比,RBD缺失-插入突变增强了细胞进入能力,尽管在第70天的样本中未检测到该突变。第48天的非刺突蛋白突变谱系在所有测试的复制子中支持最高的RNA复制效率。总体而言,等位基因频率追踪揭示了在采样时间点中出现的短暂突变和频率逐渐升高的突变。功能测试表明,体外增强的细胞进入或RNA复制并不一定预示体内持续感染。

papers.title: Recombinant Variants of SARS-CoV-2 Identified in the South of Western Siberia During the COVID-19 Pandemic
papers.abstract: Recombination is one of the mechanisms driving SARS-CoV-2 evolution and can generate genomes with novel combinations of characteristics inherited from parental lineages. We analyzed a total of 1963 genomes available SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences collected in the south of Western Siberia between March 2020 and 5 May 2023. Initial screening with Nextclade identified five potentially recombinant genomes. The consensus assemblies were re-examined by the originating laboratories and the absence of co-infection was confirmed. Recombinant origin was assessed with RecombinHunt and independently evaluated with 3SEQ and RDP5. EPI_ISL_11742584 was excluded because of numerous undetermined nucleotides. For EPI_ISL_15919275 the laboratory of origin did not confirm the reproducibility of the build. EPI_ISL_20438394 contained BA.2.35-like and XBB.3.1-like components but the signal did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Recombination was confirmed for two sequences. EPI_ISL_17317906 presumably originated from CR.1-like and XBB.1.15-like lineages and was assigned to the recombinant lineage XBV. EPI_ISL_16287253 carried a BA.2-derived segment on a BA.1-derived background. These findings indicate that automated classification should be followed by statistical validation, verification of genome assembly quality and the confirmed absence of co-infection. Incomplete and uneven genomic surveillance may still limit reconstruction of the exact origins of rare recombinant variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the presence of recombinant variants of SARS-CoV-2 in the south of Western Siberia between March 2020 and May 2023. A total of 1963 genome sequences were analyzed, and initial screening with Nextclade identified five potentially recombinant genomes. Recombinant origin was assessed using RecombinHunt, 3SEQ, and RDP5. The consensus assemblies were re-examined to confirm the absence of co-infection. Recombination was confirmed for two sequences, while other potential recombinants were excluded due to lack of reproducibility or signal survival after multiple comparisons. The study highlights the importance of statistical validation and genome assembly quality verification in identifying recombinant variants. These findings suggest that genomic surveillance may need to be more comprehensive to accurately reconstruct the origins of rare recombinant variants.

papers.title_zh: Recombinant Variants of SARS-CoV-2 Identified in the South of Western Siberia During the COVID-19 Pandemic
papers.source_body_en: Recombination is one of the mechanisms driving SARS-CoV-2 evolution and can generate genomes with novel combinations of characteristics inherited from parental lineages. We analyzed a total of 1963 genomes available SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences collected in the south of Western Siberia between March 2020 and 5 May 2023. Initial screening with Nextclade identified five potentially recombinant genomes. The consensus assemblies were re-examined by the originating laboratories and the absence of co-infection was confirmed. Recombinant origin was assessed with RecombinHunt and independently evaluated with 3SEQ and RDP5. EPI_ISL_11742584 was excluded because of numerous undetermined nucleotides. For EPI_ISL_15919275 the laboratory of origin did not confirm the reproducibility of the build. EPI_ISL_20438394 contained BA.2.35-like and XBB.3.1-like components but the signal did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Recombination was confirmed for two sequences. EPI_ISL_17317906 presumably originated from CR.1-like and XBB.1.15-like lineages and was assigned to the recombinant lineage XBV. EPI_ISL_16287253 carried a BA.2-derived segment on a BA.1-derived background. These findings indicate that automated classification should be followed by statistical validation, verification of genome assembly quality and the confirmed absence of co-infection. Incomplete and uneven genomic surveillance may still limit reconstruction of the exact origins of rare recombinant variants.

papers.title: Predictors of COVID-19 vaccination status among youth in eThekwini, South Africa: results from the AYAZAZI RIGHTS study.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Understanding which factors impact vaccine uptake is important for supporting ongoing and future vaccine programmes among youth. Objective This study examined predictors of COVID-19 vaccination uptake among South African youth in the eThekwini District. Methods Cross-sectional data from an online survey (AYAZAZI RIGHTS: December 2021–May 2022) of youth aged 18–24 in the eThekwini district, South Africa, were analyzed using a gender-stratified logistic regression of vaccination status on candidate predictors of interest (k = 14). A full model with backwards selection using Akaike’s Information Criterion was employed to remove predictors that did not add to the model’s explanatory power. Results Of 1383 participants, 54% were women, with a median sample age of 21.8 years. Overall, 37.9% (n = 525) of participants had received a COVID-19 vaccine, 58.6% of whom were women. In this cross‐sectional, observational analysis, the most consistent predictors of vaccination status were older age, living with seniors in the home, and personal proximity to severe pandemic outcomes, specifically knowing people who had been hospitalized or died due to COVID-19. Gender‐specific predictors included ethnicity, having children for women, employment, and relationship status. Conclusion Socio-demographic as well as community factors predicted receiving a COVID-19 vaccination, varying by gender. Better understanding of modifiable factors to support vaccine uptake, and curbing vaccine hesitancy related to mistrust and misinformation, will help support South Africa’s immunization programs among youth, and can help inform targeted, inclusive, and equity-oriented public-health strategies.

papers.title: Effects of XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 variant neutralisation
papers.abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to challenge strain-matched vaccination. For the 2026–27 season, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) identified XFG as the preferred antigen within the JN.1 family and Comirnaty XFG was authorised in the European Union in July, 2026. We studied 22 participants who received 30 μg of mRNA encoding XFG (Comirnaty XFG, BioNTech–Pfizer, Mainz, Germany) in September, 2026 and had paired serum available before vaccination and median 14 days afterwards. Median Wuhan-Hu-1 S1-specific IgG increased from 1600 BAU/mL (IQR 1118–2926) to 2914 BAU/mL (2117–4468), a 1·8-fold increase. Median RBD-binding ED50 increased from 116 (51·4–212) to 305·6 (170·8–434·6) for LP.8.1 and from 354·3 (129·2–558·2) to 832·9 (429–1175) for NB.1.8.1, corresponding to 2·6-fold and 2·4-fold increases, respectively (all p<0·0001). XFG-adapted vaccination increased neutralising activity against each tested variant. The GMT against XFG increased from 180 before vaccination to 894 afterwards (5·0-fold), and that against RV.1.3 increased from 121 to 599 (4·9-fold). GMTs increased from 117 to 386 for PQ.16.1.1 (3·3-fold), from 101 to 316 for XFG.1.1 (3·1-fold), from 629 to 1772 for LP.8.1 (2·8-fold), from 221 to 611 for NB.1.8.1 (2·8-fold), and from 228 to 642 for PJ.2.1 (2·8-fold). Neutralisation of BA.3.2.2 increased more modestly, from GMT 78 to 126 (1·6-fold; p=0·0009). Pre-versus post-vaccination neutralisation titres differed significantly for all variants (p<0·001). Despite the broad increase, post-vaccination neutralisation remained heterogeneous. Relative to LP.8.1, GMTs were 2·0-fold lower for XFG, 2·8-fold lower for PJ.2.1, 2·9-fold lower for NB.1.8.1, 3·0-fold lower for RV.1.3, 4·6-fold lower for PQ.16.1.1, 5·6-fold lower for XFG.1.1, and 14·1-fold lower for BA.3.2.2. These findings provide early human immunogenicity data after XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination. The largest relative increases were observed for XFG and RV.1.3, whereas LP.8.1 remained the most strongly neutralised variant after Comirnaty XFG vaccination and BA.3.2.2 the least. This pattern suggests broad boosting of cross-reactive humoral immunity without elimination of between-variant differences. The small, extensively pre-immunised cohort, short follow-up, absence of a contemporaneous vaccine-comparator group, and use of a pseudovirus assay limit inference. Our data characterise early antibody binding and neutralisation but do not establish durability or clinical effectiveness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the effects of XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 variant neutralisation, as SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to challenge strain-matched vaccination.

papers.title_zh: XFG适应性mRNA 疫苗接种对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株中和效果的研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to challenge strain-matched vaccination. For the 2026–27 season, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) identified XFG as the preferred antigen within the JN.1 family and Comirnaty XFG was authorised in the European Union in July, 2026. We studied 22 participants who received 30 μg of mRNA encoding XFG (Comirnaty XFG, BioNTech–Pfizer, Mainz, Germany) in September, 2026 and had paired serum available before vaccination and median 14 days afterwards. Median Wuhan-Hu-1 S1-specific IgG increased from 1600 BAU/mL (IQR 1118–2926) to 2914 BAU/mL (2117–4468), a 1·8-fold increase. Median RBD-binding ED50 increased from 116 (51·4–212) to 305·6 (170·8–434·6) for LP.8.1 and from 354·3 (129·2–558·2) to 832·9 (429–1175) for NB.1.8.1, corresponding to 2·6-fold and 2·4-fold increases, respectively (all p<0·0001). XFG-adapted vaccination increased neutralising activity against each tested variant. The GMT against XFG increased from 180 before vaccination to 894 afterwards (5·0-fold), and that against RV.1.3 increased from 121 to 599 (4·9-fold). GMTs increased from 117 to 386 for PQ.16.1.1 (3·3-fold), from 101 to 316 for XFG.1.1 (3·1-fold), from 629 to 1772 for LP.8.1 (2·8-fold), from 221 to 611 for NB.1.8.1 (2·8-fold), and from 228 to 642 for PJ.2.1 (2·8-fold). Neutralisation of BA.3.2.2 increased more modestly, from GMT 78 to 126 (1·6-fold; p=0·0009). Pre-versus post-vaccination neutralisation titres differed significantly for all variants (p<0·001). Despite the broad increase, post-vaccination neutralisation remained heterogeneous. Relative to LP.8.1, GMTs were 2·0-fold lower for XFG, 2·8-fold lower for PJ.2.1, 2·9-fold lower for NB.1.8.1, 3·0-fold lower for RV.1.3, 4·6-fold lower for PQ.16.1.1, 5·6-fold lower for XFG.1.1, and 14·1-fold lower for BA.3.2.2. These findings provide early human immunogenicity data after XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination. The largest relative increases were observed for XFG and RV.1.3, whereas LP.8.1 remained the most strongly neutralised variant after Comirnaty XFG vaccination and BA.3.2.2 the least. This pattern suggests broad boosting of cross-reactive humoral immunity without elimination of between-variant differences. The small, extensively pre-immunised cohort, short follow-up, absence of a contemporaneous vaccine-comparator group, and use of a pseudovirus assay limit inference. Our data characterise early antibody binding and neutralisation but do not establish durability or clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Does COVID‐19 Vaccination Protect Against Post‐COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS‐CoV‐2 infection, representing an important cause of long‐term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID‐19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post‐COVID cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID‐19 vaccination and the prevention of post‐COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model. A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. Scientific evidence indicates that COVID‐19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post‐COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. Three criteria, biological plausibility, coherence, and analogy, were partially met. Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference. COVID‐19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post‐COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post‐COVID conditions. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID‐19 vaccination in preventing post‐COVID complications.
authors: Isis Polianna Silva Ferreira de Carvalho

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the evidence for a causal relationship between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Cardiovascular diseases, including acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, are significant long-term complications of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study evaluates the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model to assess the protective role of vaccination. Evidence suggests that vaccination meets four of the nine BHC, including strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. The SCC model underscores vaccination's role as a preventive causal component. However, the evidence lacks support for specificity and experimental validation. The review highlights the need for further research to explore biological mechanisms and interactions, as well as the importance of comprehensive immunisation strategies to reduce the burden of post-COVID conditions.

papers.title: Wastewater‐Based Epidemiology for Monitoring SARS‐CoV‐2 Dynamics and Variants in Nagpur: Insights From a 16‐Month Study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This 16‐month longitudinal study in Nagpur, India, evaluated wastewater‐based epidemiology (WBE) for monitoring SARS‐CoV‐2. From March 2023 to June 2024, 1424 wastewater samples were collected from 25 urban sites; 39% were positive for SARS‐CoV‐2 RNA. Viral concentrations significantly correlated with clinical case trends ( r = 0.417; p < 0.05), closely aligning with clinical case surges, demonstrating its utility as a complementary surveillance tool. Sequencing of 69 genomes revealed multiple lineages, including prevalent VOIs like BA.2.86 and XBB.1.16, alongside lower abundance variants. No high‐impact VOCs were detected. Unique local mutational patterns in ORF1ab and Spike genes, including rare stop‐gain and frame shift mutations, suggest ongoing viral evolution. Environmental factors did not significantly influence detection. WBE is a feasible tool for public health, enabling early outbreak detection and genomic surveillance for future SARS‐CoV‐2 threats.

The findings support the use of WBE for early outbreak detection and genomic surveillance, which can aid public health preparedness. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 本研究在印度那格浦尔市进行了一项为期16个月的纵向研究,评估基于污水的流行病学(WBE)用于监测严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)的可行性。从2023年3月至2024年6月,从那格浦尔市25个城市地点收集了1424份污水样本;其中39%检测出严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RNA。病毒浓度与临床病例趋势显著相关(r = 0.417;p < 0.05),与临床病例激增紧密一致,表明其作为补充监测工具的有效性。对69个基因组进行测序,揭示了多种病毒谱系,包括常见的关注变异株(VOIs)如BA.2.86和XBB.1.16,以及低丰度变异株。未检测到高影响的变异株关切株(VOCs)。在ORF1ab和刺突蛋白基因中观察到独特的本地突变模式,包括罕见的停止增益和移码突变突变,表明病毒正在持续进化进化。环境因素未显著影响检测结果。基于污水的监测(WBE)是公共卫生可行的工具,能够实现早期暴发检测和基因组监测,为未来严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2威胁提供预警信息。

papers.title: Variation in social contact levels and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic by occupation and socio-economic status in east Zimbabwe
papers.abstract: Background: COVID-19 movement restrictions reduced social contact worldwide, curbing viral spread but with unequal economic consequences where social safety nets are limited. Little evidence exists on how these impacts varied by occupation, wealth and age in resource-constrained settings. This paper examined pre-pandemic contact and lockdown-related change. Methods: The paper documents analysis of a population-representative survey (N=8,499) in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown. Negative binomial regression models assessed pre-lockdown contact counts by socio-economic characteristics, overall and by place (home, school, work, transport, entertainment); linear regression assessed predictors of lockdown declines. Results: Pre-COVID-19, respondents reported a median of 12 daily contacts (interquartile range [IQR] 4-47), with higher counts among manual labourers (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.00, 2.44), retail and public sector workers (IRR 2.33, 95%CI 2.09, 2.60) and students (IRR 2.59, 95%CI 2.38, 2.82), males, wealthier respondents, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents. Counts were highest in schools. During lockdown, contacts fell across all subgroups to a median of 8 (IQR 4-28). Declines were greatest among those with most pre-COVID-19 contacts: urban (mean -17.5, 95%CI -19.53, -15.37) and agricultural estate residents (-18.1, 95%CI -19.99, -16.13), students and teachers (-17.7, 95%CI -19.82, -15.59), males and 30-44 year olds. Drops were greatest in schools and on transport. Conclusion: Reductions in contact under blanket lockdown varied markedly between subgroups and places in Manicaland, Zimbabwe. Selectively targeting high-contact groups might have achieved similar transmission reductions while limiting economic damage, holding lessons for similar settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how social contact levels varied by occupation and socio-economic status during the COVID-19 pandemic in east Zimbabwe, as movement restrictions had uneven economic consequences in resource-constrained settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a population-representative survey (N=8,499) conducted in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression models assessed pre-lockdown contact counts by socio-economic characteristics, overall and by place (home, school, work, transport, entertainment); linear regression assessed predictors of lockdown declines.
analysis.main_results: Pre-COVID-19, respondents reported a median of 12 daily contacts (interquartile range [IQR] 4-47), with higher counts among manual labourers, retail and public sector workers, students, males, wealthier respondents, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents. Counts were highest in schools. During lockdown, contacts fell across all subgroups to a median of 8 (IQR 4-28). Declines were greatest among those with most pre-COVID-19 contacts: urban and agricultural estate residents, students and teachers, males and 30-44 year olds. Drops were greatest in schools and on transport.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that reductions in contact under blanket lockdown varied markedly between subgroups and places in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, highlighting the need for targeted interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for reducing viral transmission in resource-constrained settings by identifying high-contact groups and places that could be prioritized for targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a single region in Zimbabwe, but the evidence is strong due to the use of regression models and a representative sample.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated variation in social contact levels and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic by occupation and socio-economic status in east Zimbabwe. It analyzed a population-representative survey of 8,499 individuals conducted during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first lockdown. The results showed that pre-pandemic contact levels were higher among manual labourers, retail and public sector workers, students, males, wealthier individuals, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents, with the highest counts observed in schools. During lockdown, contact levels decreased across all subgroups, with the most significant drops among those with the highest pre-lockdown contact levels, particularly in schools and transport. The authors concluded that targeted interventions for high-contact groups could achieve similar transmission reductions with less economic damage, offering insights for similar settings. The study's reliance on self-reported data and regional focus limits its generalizability, but the use of regression models and a representative sample supports its findings.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a population-representative survey (N=8,499) conducted in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown.
elements_en.methods: Negative binomial regression models assessed pre-lockdown contact counts by socio-economic characteristics, overall and by place (home, school, work, transport, entertainment); linear regression assessed predictors of lockdown declines.
elements_en.main_results: Pre-COVID-19, respondents reported a median of 12 daily contacts (interquartile range [IQR] 4-47), with higher counts among manual labourers, retail and public sector workers, students, males, wealthier respondents, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents. Counts were highest in schools. During lockdown, contacts fell across all subgroups to a median of 8 (IQR 4-28). Declines were greatest among those with most pre-COVID-19 contacts: urban and agricultural estate residents, students and teachers, males and 30-44 year olds. Drops were greatest in schools and on transport.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that reductions in contact under blanket lockdown varied markedly between subgroups and places in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, highlighting the need for targeted interventions.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for reducing viral transmission in resource-constrained settings by identifying high-contact groups and places that could be prioritized for targeted interventions.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a single region in Zimbabwe, but the evidence is strong due to the use of regression models and a representative sample.

papers.title_zh: Variation in social contact levels and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic by occupation and socio-economic status in east Zimbabwe
papers.source_body_en: Background: COVID-19 movement restrictions reduced social contact worldwide, curbing viral spread but with unequal economic consequences where social safety nets are limited. Little evidence exists on how these impacts varied by occupation, wealth and age in resource-constrained settings. This paper examined pre-pandemic contact and lockdown-related change. Methods: The paper documents analysis of a population-representative survey (N=8,499) in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown. Negative binomial regression models assessed pre-lockdown contact counts by socio-economic characteristics, overall and by place (home, school, work, transport, entertainment); linear regression assessed predictors of lockdown declines. Results: Pre-COVID-19, respondents reported a median of 12 daily contacts (interquartile range [IQR] 4-47), with higher counts among manual labourers (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 2.21, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.00, 2.44), retail and public sector workers (IRR 2.33, 95%CI 2.09, 2.60) and students (IRR 2.59, 95%CI 2.38, 2.82), males, wealthier respondents, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents. Counts were highest in schools. During lockdown, contacts fell across all subgroups to a median of 8 (IQR 4-28). Declines were greatest among those with most pre-COVID-19 contacts: urban (mean -17.5, 95%CI -19.53, -15.37) and agricultural estate residents (-18.1, 95%CI -19.99, -16.13), students and teachers (-17.7, 95%CI -19.82, -15.59), males and 30-44 year olds. Drops were greatest in schools and on transport. Conclusion: Reductions in contact under blanket lockdown varied markedly between subgroups and places in Manicaland, Zimbabwe. Selectively targeting high-contact groups might have achieved similar transmission reductions while limiting economic damage, holding lessons for similar settings.

papers.title: Demand Promotion Interventions to Improve COVID-19 Vaccine Uptake: A Systematic Review of the Global Evidence
papers.abstract: Background: /Objectives: The global rollout of COVID-19 vaccines faced significant implementation challenges: limited adult immunization infrastructure, particularly in low- and middle-income countries; rapidly shifting viral epidemiology driven by emerging variants; and widespread vaccine misinformation that fueled hesitancy. Achieving the high coverage necessary to curb transmission required urgent attention to demand-side barriers, making the identification of effective interventions a critical public health priority. This systematic review synthesized global evidence on communication, behavioral, and health systems interventions to increase COVID-19 vaccine demand and uptake. The review assessed intervention effectiveness across diverse population groups and settings and identified lessons to inform the design of adult vaccination programs and future outbreak response. Methods: Between March 2022 and July 2024, we performed a systematic search in PubMed, Scopus, and Global Index Medicus, for COVID-19 demand and uptake studies published after December 2020, with no language or geographic restrictions. Eligible papers were those that reported intervention studies with quantitative comparative outcomes on vaccination attitudes, appointment rates, uptake, or coverage following an intervention. Study quality was assessed using adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Program (CASP) criteria. Studies were categorized into nine intervention approaches, based on an adapted communication and service-delivery taxonomy. Interventions operated at individual, systems, and structural levels. A narrative synthesis was combined with vote counting of studies with positive findings to understand what intervention approaches were effective. and under what conditions. Results: From over 23,000 records, 57 studies from 27 countries met inclusion and quality criteria. Most studies were conducted in high-income countries. Overall, 70% of studies reported positive findings on at least one vaccination outcome. analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines demand-side interventions to improve SARS-CoV-2 vaccine uptake globally. It highlights the challenges of limited immunization infrastructure, shifting viral epidemiology, and vaccine misinformation. The review identifies educational, access-enhancing, and service delivery interventions as effective, with mandates showing strong effects but raising ethical concerns. These insights are valuable for future outbreak preparedness and adult immunization programs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述旨在识别有效的促进需求的干预措施,以提高严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗的全球接种率,应对诸如成人免疫接种基础设施有限、病毒流行病学快速变化以及疫苗错误信息等挑战。核心问题聚焦于理解沟通、行为和卫生系统干预措施在提高疫苗接种需求和接种率方面的有效性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述在2022年3月至2024年7月期间对PubMed、Scopus和Global Index Medicus进行了系统搜索,包括2020年12月之后发表的研究,无语言或地理限制。研究质量使用改编的Critical Appraisal Skills Program(CASP)标准进行评估。根据改编的沟通和服务交付分类学,将干预措施分为九种方法。通过叙述性综合和对具有积极结果的研究进行投票计数的方法来评估干预措施的有效性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述发现,70%的研究报告了至少一项疫苗接种结果的积极发现。当通过多个渠道由值得信赖的传播者传递,并与互补策略相结合时,教育干预措施效果最佳。增强可及性和服务交付干预措施显示出最一致的有效性证据,其中十项研究中有九项报告了积极结果。疫苗强制措施在大规模覆盖率方面显示出最强且最一致的效果,尽管它们引发了伦理问题。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 提醒和推动干预措施的结果混杂,表现最佳的是当它们嵌入到多成分干预措施中。综述指出,大多数研究是在高收入国家进行的,这在低收入和中等收入环境中留下了证据缺口。此外,关于干预措施在特定人群或地区中的有效性信息也有限。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 政策制定者应优先考虑增强可及性和加强系统干预作为基础,补充以值得信赖的传播者提供的针对性沟通,并仅在较不严格的措施已被证明不足的情况下保留强制措施。这些发现不仅适用于疫情,也为成人免疫接种项目和未来的暴发准备提供了相关性。

papers.title: Mental health and healthcare use during COVID‐19 among neurodivergent youth and youth with pre‐existing psychiatric disorders: A systematic review
papers.abstract: Neurodivergent youth and youth with pre‐existing psychiatric disorders may have faced additional challenges in navigating the demands and restrictions of the COVID‐19 pandemic. However, less is known about how mental health outcomes and psychiatric healthcare utilization differed across diagnostic groups and other youth‐related factors. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on mental health symptoms and psychiatric healthcare use among youth with pre‐existing conditions during the pandemic. We searched PubMed, Web of Science and additional sources for cross‐sectional and longitudinal studies with data collected between March 2020 and May 2023. Eligible studies included neurodivergent youth and/or youth with psychiatric disorders confirmed through clinician diagnosis or medical records prior to the pandemic. Given the clinical and methodological diversity of studies, findings were synthesized narratively. Forty‐eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Mental health outcomes showed mixed patterns both across and within diagnostic groups, with individual studies reporting symptom increase, stability and improvements. Evidence on psychiatric healthcare utilization was more limited and suggested different patterns between service use and psychotropic medication use. Compared to boys, girls were more likely to experience COVID‐related distress and increases in psychiatric service use during the pandemic. Age‐related findings varied across developmental stages and outcome domains. Most studies ( n = 40; 83.3%) had a moderate overall risk of bias (RoB), while seven (14.6%) had a high overall RoB. Mental health outcomes among youth with pre‐existing conditions during the COVID‐19 pandemic varied both within and across diagnostic groups. Outcomes were also associated with individual, developmental, contextual and service‐related factors. These findings suggest the importance of considering such factors alongside diagnosis when identifying clinical needs and planning support during large‐scale societal disruptions. Evidence on psychiatric healthcare utilization remains limited. More methodologically robust research is needed to clarify mental health and healthcare‐use patterns during major public health emergencies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines mental health symptoms and psychiatric healthcare use among neurodivergent youth and those with pre-existing psychiatric disorders during the COVID-19 pandemic. The review includes 48 studies, with most having a moderate risk of bias. Mental health outcomes varied across and within diagnostic groups, showing mixed patterns of symptom increase, stability, and improvement. Evidence on healthcare utilization was limited, with differing patterns observed between service use and medication use. Girls were more likely to experience distress and increased service use compared to boys. Age-related findings varied across developmental stages and outcome domains. The review highlights the need for more robust research to better understand these patterns during public health emergencies.

papers.title: Data Reduction in SARS-CoV-2 Amplicon Sequencing: Effects of Read Subsampling and Normalization on Consensus Quality, Lineage Assignment, and Computational Burden
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Amplicon-based next-generation sequencing is a cornerstone of viral genomic surveillance, but it often produces datasets with highly uneven read coverage due to PCR amplification bias. This leads to excessive data generation and substantial computational overhead for downstream bioinformatic analysis. Results We evaluated the efficacy of two data reduction strategies on 220 SARS-CoV-2 clinical specimens and 12 wastewater samples: random subsampling with SeqKit and read depth normalization with BBNorm. FASTQ files were reduced to target depths from 10X to 10,000X to compare genome coverage, lineage assignment concordance, and computational resource usage. Both strategies markedly reduced total processing time. For clinical isolates, read depth normalization corrected for amplification bias resulting in highly concordant lineage assignments at a target depth of just 200X. Random subsampling preserved inherent bias but produced reliable assignments at depths over 500X. Reducing target depths below 500X in complex wastewater mixtures severely degraded variant deconvolution accuracy and heavily skewed lineage abundance profiles for both methods. Conclusion Both random subsampling and read depth normalization successfully reduce computational overhead while preserving key clinical sequencing metrics at appropriate reduction settings. The optimal method depends on the analytical goal, ranging from computationally lightweight random subsampling for rapid lineage assignment, to read depth normalization for generating high-quality consensus sequences. However, aggressive data reduction should be avoided in environmental surveillance, where maintaining a high baseline sequencing depth is critical for accurate mixed-variant deconvolution.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 基于扩增子的下一代测序是病毒基因组监测的核心技术,但由于PCR扩增偏差,它经常产生读取覆盖度高度不均的数据集。这导致了数据生成过多以及下游生物信息学分析的计算负担显著增加。结果 我们评估了两种数据缩减策略在220个严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2临床样本和12个污水样本中的效果:使用SeqKit进行随机子采样和使用BBNorm进行读取深度归一化。将FASTQ文件缩减到目标深度从10X到10,000X,以比较基因组的覆盖度、谱系分配一致性以及计算资源使用情况。两种策略都显著减少了总处理时间。对于临床分离株,读取深度归一化校正了扩增偏差,使得在仅200X的目标深度下谱系分配高度一致。随机子采样保留了固有的偏差,但在超过500X的深度下仍能产生可靠的分配结果。在复杂的污水混合物中,将目标深度降低至500X以下会严重降低变异株解卷积的准确性,并且对两种方法的谱系丰度分布产生显著偏差。结论 随机子采样和读取深度归一化在适当的缩减设置下,成功地减少了计算负担,同时保留了关键的临床测序指标。最佳方法取决于分析目标,从计算负担较轻的随机子采样用于快速谱系分配,到读取深度归一化用于生成高质量的共识序列。然而,在环境监测中应避免激进的数据缩减,因为在这些情况下,保持较高的基础测序深度对于准确的混合变异株解卷积至关重要。

papers.title: Epidemiology and virological characteristics of the emerging SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate globally at high levels and to evolve into new variants. Recently, a new saltation variant harbouring a highly mutated spike protein, PJ.2.1, emerged in North America. Here, we provide a brief epidemiological and virological characterization of PJ.2.1 and cocirculating variants. We report that PJ.2.1 is spreading in the USA, Canada, and Spain and mainly infects individuals aged 60 years and older, as do most other variants, with the exception of BA.3.2, which preferentially infects individuals aged 0-9 years. PJ.2.1 was less susceptible to inhibition by an antibody against ACE2 than were the other variants, indicating increased ACE2 binding. In contrast, PJ.2.1 did not show augmented evasion of antibodies from vaccinees who had received the LP.8.1-adapted vaccine compared with most other variants analysed. These results suggest that augmented ACE2 affinity rather than increased antibody evasion might drive the current, rapid spread of PJ.2.1.

We report that PJ.2.1 is spreading in the USA, Canada, and Spain and mainly infects individuals aged 60 years and older, as do most other variants, with the exception of BA.3.2, which preferentially infects individuals aged 0-9 years. In contrast, PJ.2.1 did not show augmented evasion of antibodies from vaccinees who had received the LP.8.1-adapted vaccine compared with most other variants analysed. papers.abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2持续在全球范围内高水平传播并进化出新的变种。最近,在北美出现了一种新的跳跃变种PJ.2.1,其携带高度突变的刺突蛋白。本文简要介绍了PJ.2.1及其他同时传播变种的流行病学和病毒学特征。我们报告称,PJ.2.1在美国、加拿大和西班牙传播,并主要感染60岁及以上人群,与其他大多数变种类似,但BA.3.2则更倾向于感染0-9岁人群。PJ.2.1对针对ACE2的抗体抑制作用较弱,与其他变种相比显示出更高的ACE2结合能力。相比之下,PJ.2.1并未表现出比大多数其他分析变种更强的对接受LP.8.1适应株疫苗免疫的个体的抗体逃逸能力。这些结果表明,增强的ACE2亲和力而非增加的抗体逃逸能力可能驱动了PJ.2.1当前的快速传播。

papers.title: Anesthesia as a Partner in Public Health: Enabling National Pediatric SARS-CoV-2 Serosurveillance in Australia
papers.abstract: Anesthetic departments played a critical role in Australia’s COVID-19 response by facilitating the collection of residual blood samples from children undergoing elective procedures. Through a partnership with the Pediatric Active Enhanced Disease Surveillance network, this approach enabled three national SARS-CoV-2 serosurveys between 2020 and 2023. It provided an ethical, feasible, and nationally representative method for assessing infection- and vaccine-derived immunity in children, a population in whom routine blood sampling is difficult and from whom residual blood samples are not commonly available. The resulting data informed COVID-19 vaccination policy, improved understanding of infection burden and immunity, and contributed to broader public health decision-making. This experience demonstrates how anesthetic departments can extend their impact beyond perioperative care, serving as essential partners in public health surveillance and research.

papers.title: Prognostic implications of asymptomatic COVID-19 infection in non-small-cell lung cancer patients receiving active anticancer treatment: an observational study with prospective survival follow-up.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We previously reported that non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was a significant predictor of delayed viral clearance from their COVID-19 infection during the Omicron variant attack between January and April 2022. We now evaluated the survival outcomes of these NSCLC patients with or without COVID-19 infection during this period. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 276 NSCLC patients recruited. Of them, 39 patients were SARS-CoV-2 positive through PCR testing, with viral load indicated by cycle threshold (ct) values. Propensity score matching was used to ensure the COVID-positive and COVID-negative groups were comparable in demographics, disease staging, and treatment modalities. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression were performed to evaluate overall survival and identify OS prognostic factors. RESULTS: After a median follow up of 39.9 months from diagnosis (interquartile range 31.3-55.5), 20 died of COVID-19 and NSCLC. OS differences counting from either their NSCLC diagnosis, or the start of anticancer treatment were insignificant among various stages of NSCLC patients infected with COVID-19, but they were significant for COVID-negative patients (P = 0.050 and P = 0.009, respectively). Exploratory analysis revealed that ct value cutoff of > 34.14 correlated with a better OS (P = 0.039). Multivariable analysis identified chemotherapy (P = 0.002), immune checkpoint inhibitor (P = 0.019), and receipt of ≥ 2 doses of COVID-19 vaccines (P = 0.011) as significant prognosticators of OS, counting from the date of anticancer treatment. CONCLUSION: Asymptomatic COVID-19 infection might compromise survival outcomes of NSCLC patients in this study. Closer attention may be needed.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study investigated the survival outcomes of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with or without asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron variant attack in 2022. A prospective cohort of 276 NSCLC patients was followed for a median of 39.9 months, with 39 testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 via PCR. Propensity score matching was used to compare groups, and survival analysis revealed that OS differences were significant for COVID-negative patients but not for those infected with SARS-CoV-2. Exploratory analysis suggested a ct value cutoff of > 34.14 correlated with better OS. The authors concluded that asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection may negatively impact survival outcomes in NSCLC patients, emphasizing the need for closer monitoring. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational nature, though the use of matching and survival analysis strengthens its validity.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2-Specific IgG Levels Are Inversely Associated with ACPA-Reactive Pathological and Natural Autoantibody Profiles in Residual Diagnostic Samples
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels vary among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the most prevalent SARD, this is further shaped by rheumatoid factors (RFs). Attenuated post-vaccination antibody levels in RA are documented, but links to broader autoreactivity remain underexplored. We therefore examined pathological (pAAbs) and natural autoantibodies (nAAbs) in relation to SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG. Methods: A decade-long dataset (2014–2024; 73,747 patients) gave descriptive context, not the substudy population. SARS-CoV-2 IgG and nAAbs were evaluated in 200 residual specimens collected between November 2023 and February 2024. SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG was interpreted as an antiviral readout, not a protection correlate (clinical/exposure data unavailable). QuantiVac (wild-type) and Omicron BA.1 IgG were compared across ACPA-reactive (n = 44/38), anti-SSA/SSB-dominant (n = 24/22), anti-dsDNA-reactive (n = 33/32), aPL AAb-dominant (n = 15/14), and autoantibody-negative groups (n = 70/68). Results: ACPA-reactive samples showed lower antiviral IgG across both assays. After age/sex adjustment, comparator groups had 2.58–3.30-fold higher QuantiVac and 2.70–4.87-fold higher Omicron BA.1 IgG. Antiviral IgG correlated inversely with ACPA IgG (ρ to −0.474) and RF isotypes (ρ = −0.299 to −0.400). ACPA-reactive samples showed increased CS-IgM and HSP60/HSP70 IgG/IgM reactivity, which correlated positively with ACPA IgG and RF isotypes. Conclusions: In this exploratory analysis, an ACPA-reactive serological profile was associated with lower SARS-CoV-2 IgG and higher, positively correlated CS- and HSP-directed autoantibody levels, suggesting a shared rather than independent basis for these autoreactive compartments. These cross-sectional associations persisted after age/sex adjustment but cannot be separated from unmeasured clinical, treatment, or exposure factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG levels and autoantibody profiles in patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), particularly rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The research highlights that ACPA-reactive samples exhibit lower antiviral IgG levels compared to other groups, with significant inverse correlations observed between SARS-CoV-2 IgG and ACPA IgG or RF isotypes. The findings suggest a potential shared basis for these autoreactive compartments rather than independent mechanisms. However, the study acknowledges limitations, as the cross-sectional associations may be influenced by unmeasured clinical, treatment, or exposure factors. The results contribute to understanding the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 immunity and autoantibody profiles in RA, offering insights into the complex immune responses in autoimmune conditions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景/目的:在系统性自身免疫风湿性疾病(SARDs)患者中,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2特异性抗体水平存在差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在类风湿性关节炎(RA)中,这是最常见的SARDs,这种差异进一步受到类风湿因子(RFs)的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 一个十年期的数据集(2014–2024;73,747名患者)提供了描述性背景,而非子研究人群。在2023年11月至2024年2月期间收集的200份残留样本中评估了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG和nAAbs。将严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2特异性IgG解释为抗病毒药物的读数,而非保护相关因素(临床/暴露数据不可用)。
elements_zh.main_results: ACPA反应性样本在两种检测中均表现出较低的抗病毒药物 IgG水平。在调整年龄和性别后,对照组的QuantiVac IgG水平高出2.58–3.30倍,Omicron BA.1 IgG水平高出2.70–4.87倍。抗病毒药物 IgG与ACPA IgG(ρ至−0.474)以及RF亚型(ρ = −0.299至−0.400)呈负相关。ACPA反应性样本表现出增加的CS-IgM和HSP60/HSP70 IgG/IgM反应性,这些反应性与ACPA IgG和RF亚型呈正相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项探索性分析中,ACPA反应性血清学谱型与较低的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG水平以及较高、正相关的CS和HSP定向自身抗体水平相关,提示这些自身反应性组分可能具有共同而非独立的基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在RA中已记录到疫苗接种后抗体水平减弱,但与更广泛的自身反应性之间的联系仍待深入研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些横断面关联在调整年龄和性别后仍然存在,但无法排除未测量的临床、治疗或暴露因素的影响。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目的:在系统性自身免疫风湿性疾病(SARDs)患者中,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2特异性抗体水平存在差异。在最常见SARDs——类风湿性关节炎(RA)中,这种差异进一步受到类风湿因子(RFs)的影响。在RA中已记录到疫苗接种后抗体水平减弱,但与更广泛的自身反应性之间的联系仍待深入研究。因此,我们考察了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2特异性IgG与病理(pAAbs)和天然自身抗体(nAAbs)之间的关系。方法:一个十年期的数据集(2014–2024;73,747名患者)提供了描述性背景,而非子研究人群。在2023年11月至2024年2月期间收集的200份残留样本中评估了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG和nAAbs。将严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2特异性IgG解释为抗病毒药物的读数,而非保护相关因素(临床/暴露数据不可用)。比较了QuantiVac(野生型)和Omicron BA.1 IgG在ACPA反应性(n = 44/38)、抗SSA/SSB主导(n = 24/22)、抗dsDNA反应性(n = 33/32)、aPL AAb主导(n = 15/14)以及自身抗体阴性组(n = 70/68)中的水平。结果:ACPA反应性样本在两种检测中均表现出较低的抗病毒药物 IgG水平。在调整年龄和性别后,对照组的QuantiVac IgG水平高出2.58–3.30倍,Omicron BA.1 IgG水平高出2.70–4.87倍。抗病毒药物 IgG与ACPA IgG(ρ至−0.474)以及RF亚型(ρ = −0.299至−0.400)呈负相关。ACPA反应性样本表现出增加的CS-IgM和HSP60/HSP70 IgG/IgM反应性,这些反应性与ACPA IgG和RF亚型呈正相关。结论:在这项探索性分析中,ACPA反应性血清学谱型与较低的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG水平以及较高、正相关的CS和HSP定向自身抗体水平相关,提示这些自身反应性组分可能具有共同而非独立的基础。这些横断面关联在调整年龄和性别后仍然存在,但无法排除未测量的临床、治疗或暴露因素的影响。
